acme_prod: Hey team — we have a surprising invoice jump (~$1.8k) for INV-ACME-2789 (Feb). Usage dashboard shows ~2.7M tokens but our internal app logs show ~1.3M. It lines up with heavy streaming use and a bunch of client reconnects. Suspect duplicate token accounting when clients abort mid-stream and immediately reconnect.

ana-support: Sorry about this — can you paste the invoice id, time range, and any request/session ids you have?

acme_prod: Invoice INV-ACME-2789, timeframe 2026-02-01 -> 2026-02-28. Example session id: sess_9bf2c, request id X-Request-Id: r-32d. Quick repro steps we used: 
1) Start SSE stream to /v1/generate with session_id=sess_9bf2c
2) stream until ~600 tokens
3) client does xhr.abort() at token ~602 (user cancels)
4) client instantly reconnects and resumes with same session_id -> server continues and totals ~1200 tokens, dashboard shows 1200 billed, but app-level accounting only counted 600 before cancel.

jordan-eng: can you paste a minimal SSE chunk sequence? e.g.:
```
data: {"delta":"...", "tokens":600}

data: [CANCELLED]

data: {"delta":"...","tokens":602}
```

acme_prod: Attached a capture. Raw logs from our side: 
```
[2026-02-18T14:12:21Z] sess_9bf2c connection closed by client (xhr abort)
[2026-02-18T14:12:21Z] sess_9bf2c partial_kv_flush tokens=602
[2026-02-18T14:12:22Z] sess_9bf2c new connection from same client -> resumed
[2026-02-18T14:12:22Z] sess_9bf2c resumed_kv_restore tokens=0
[2026-02-18T14:12:22Z] sess_9bf2c generate tokens=1200
```

jordan-eng: thanks. That pattern points at the resume/finalize flow. If the runtime marks the partial_kv_flush on close but the resume path doesn't mark those tokens as already-billed or doesn't rehydrate a finalized offset, we can end up charging again when the resumed connection generates the rest. Two initial questions: 1) is the client intentionally reusing the same session_id to continue a single conversation? 2) did the client send any explicit finalize or done event before aborting?

acme_prod: Yes, client reuses session_id to continue a conversation (we call it a persistent convo id). There is no explicit "finalize" event on abort — it's an immediate abort. Expected behavior: server should allow resume without double-billing (i.e., detect earlier partial tokens and not charge twice).

kevin-billing: looping in billing ops. @acme_prod can you share the line items CSV for INV-ACME-2789 (we need timestamps + request ids). We'll run an allocation audit and check for duplicate token entries. Also confirm the API key suffix if possible (last 4) so we can filter logs.

ana-support: Opening a support ticket and assigning to eng. SUP-5789 created. Tags: billing, streaming, metering-drift.

jordan-eng: assigning to me. First steps: reproduce with a curl+abort scenario and instrument token-meter to emit "finalize" events per connection. I want to trace whether the resumed path calls the same meter or spins up a new meter instance. If the latter, tokens could be double-counted. Noting runtime change: v3.15 changed KV-cache resurrection timing which might affect resume semantics.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: inference-runtime v3.14 -> v3.15 at 2026-02-20T03:00:00Z (sha: a1b2c3d)

jordan-eng: runtime v3.15 changed KV cache resurrection behavior — plausible root cause. I'll add instrumentation and a repro harness.

kevin-billing: if eng confirms double-count for specific sessions, billing can issue a one-time credit. Please DM me the CSV export and SUP-5789 link.

acme_prod: sending a small HAR + curl snippet in SUP-5789. Sample curl we used to reproduce: 
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer ak-XXXX-d4f2" -d '{"session_id":"sess_9bf2c","model":"xlarge","prompt":"..."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
# then sleep 0.5; pkill -f curl (simulate abort)
# reconnect immediately with same session_id
```

ana-support: Thanks, we'll keep you posted in SUP-5789. If anyone else noticed usage spikes after 2026-02-20 (post-deploy) please reply here so we can correlate. :eyes:

jordan-eng: quick note: temporary mitigations are on the table — 1) server-side resume dedupe (mark partial ranges as billed), 2) doc change advising SDKs to emit explicit finalize on cancel, or 3) short-term billing forgiveness for affected customers while we patch. I'll prototype option #1 and share findings.

kevin-billing: agreed. Once eng confirms the pattern and affected sessions, billing will coordinate credits.

acme_prod: huge thanks for fast response. We'll monitor and share any more examples. :pray:
